Reviewer view: the judge's full reasoning

To both parties: this dispute is about the SGD 4.50 cancellation fee charged on trip TRP-02744 after the driver cancelled at 08:17:36 under the reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW.

How to appeal: You may appeal once within 30 days (POL-GEN-04). A different human reviewer hears it, and only record evidence may be added.

POL-GEN-05: the monetary effect is SGD 4.50 against an execution threshold of SGD 8.00. It does not exceed the threshold, so the amount is executed automatically on issue, subject to POL-GEN-04.

Read POL-GEN-04 in full
Every ruling issued without human review is a provisional ruling. Either party may appeal it once, within 30 days of the trip or of the ruling's issue, whichever is later, by lodging the appeal with the platform's help channel. An appeal (a) is heard by a human reviewer who did not take part in any earlier review of the same trip; (b) may add only record-type evidence - a GPS export, a fare or payment statement, an ERP gantry record with gantry name, entry time and cashcard statement, a call log, a photograph with its capture time - and may not add or amend a party statement; (c) suspends execution of any amount not yet executed and freezes it until decided, and where the amount was executed under POL-GEN-05 before the appeal, a successful appeal reverses it; (d) may not be withdrawn and re-lodged. A second appeal on the same trip, an appeal lodged after 30 days, or an appeal that adds only statements is refused. The appeal decision is recorded as a human closure under POL-GEN-06, enters the precedent store, and is final on the platform. This clause licenses no ruling value: an appeal is a route to human review, not a ruling, and it is lodged after a ruling has issued.

Each draft's own explanation

Draft 1 - sampled
To both parties: this dispute is about the SGD 4.50 cancellation fee charged on trip TRP-02744 after the driver cancelled at 08:17:36 under the reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW. The fee is chargeable only if all four conditions of POL-NS-01 hold. Two of them fail on the driver's own evidence. Condition (b) requires the GPS trace (EV-GPS-02744) to place the driver inside the pickup geofence, which POL-NS-02 sets at 50 m for this STANDARD pickup (trip_record.pickup_zone_class in EV-TRIP-02744): at least three consecutive fixes inside 50 m, each accurate to 25 m or better. That trace is COMPLETE, 98 fixes at a 10-second cadence with no gaps, and the derived count of qualifying in-radius fixes is 0; the driver's closest approach anywhere in the trace is 53.84 m. Condition (c) requires an in-geofence dwell of at least the 180-second free waiting period in force (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec = 180), measured from the first qualifying in-geofence fix; that dwell is 0 seconds. The 'I'm Here' button press at 08:11:35 does not start that clock: POL-NS-01(c) runs it from the GPS fix, and POL-NS-12, which lets the platform's own arrival and wait-timer events stand in for the trace, applies only where trip_record.platform_policy.arrival_marker is GPS_AUTO, and here it is BUTTON. The six-minute wait timer therefore records a tap, not an arrival, and there is no reading of the trace on which this fee is earned. POL-NS-05 (false arrival marker) is not established either way and I make no finding under it. The derived facts report no distance and no speed for the driver at the 08:11:35 marker, so the clause's trigger - more than 300 m from the pin, or 15 km/h or more, at the marker's timestamp - cannot be tested. The 53.84 m figure the Driver Advocate relies on is the minimum across the whole trace, not the position at the marker; it is well inside POL-NS-05's 300 m leash, but it neither proves nor disproves a false marker at 08:11:35. Because no false-arrival finding is made, no POL-NS-05(ii) referral is recorded; a referral exists only where a clause produces one. On the Driver Advocate's submission that this is a POL-NS-03 wrong-position case: accepted to this extent. A closest approach of 53.84 m lies outside the 50 m radius but inside POL-NS-03's 400 m ceiling, so on the driver's own account he came to the venue and held just outside the radius rather than never arriving. That does not change the money. POL-NS-03 refunds the cancellation fee to the rider in full, and its only two compensation routes are closed on this record. Route (i) needs the rider to have given the correct entrance, block, tower or bay in the chat log and the driver not to have moved to it, and the chat (EV-CHAT-02744) holds only the driver's 'here' at 08:11:55 and the rider's 'ok' at 08:13:05 - no sub-location from either party. Route (ii) needs trip_record.registered_pickup_points of 2 or more, and this trip registers exactly 1. The Rider Advocate reached the same conclusion in the alternative, and it is right. Switching to POL-NS-02 makes no difference: where the trace contains no qualifying in-radius fix in the 15 minutes before the cancellation, the driver never arrived, limb (b) fails, and the fee is refunded in full. Both routes land on a full refund and neither produces driver compensation, so the choice between them does not affect the outcome. Under POL-NS-06 the same result follows from the arithmetic: the effective dwell is 0 seconds against the 180-second minimum, so the fee is not chargeable and is refunded in full whether or not the rider was present and whether or not she replied to messages. The one route by which the driver could have accumulated separate in-geofence intervals - POL-NS-06(i) - is closed: the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-02744-01 is MISSING (weight_multiplier 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT, payload null), and the clause makes limb (i) unavailable where the advisory is missing. There is therefore no lawful-holding excuse and no accumulation. POL-NS-04 does not need to be reached, and it does not exonerate the rider: her only message, 'ok' at 08:13:05, names no position, entrance, block, tower or bay, asks for the driver's position, and does not say she cannot see the vehicle, so limb (a) fails at its first requirement. That does not matter, because the refund follows from the driver's trace, not from this clause. The Rider Advocate's further point that the rider was at the pickup point throughout is factually supported - EV-GPS-02744's rider_presence block shows 69 fixes, every one qualifying, all stationary, never more than 13.59 m from the pin - and it sits badly with a RIDER_NO_SHOW termination, but the fee falls on the driver's own trace test and I rest nothing on it. The driver's statement in the dispute record that he 'was right at the pin' carries no weight_multiplier, is contradicted by his own trace, and is not used as a carrier of any fact. Driver compensation is not payable. POL-NS-07 pays the driver only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full or POL-NS-10(g) applies; neither does, and POL-NS-06 displaces the fee, so the 80 per cent payout of SGD 3.60 the Driver Advocate computes is conditional on a premise that fails. For completeness, the anti-farming check does not trip on the two figures the clause names - driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 2, below the 4 required, and 2 divided by driver_profile.completed_trips_30d of 91 is a rate of 0.022, below the 0.08 threshold - but that is not reached, because compensation is not owed in the first place. Those are the only profile fields used, as POL-GEN-01 requires. Amount and integrity. EV-FARE-02744 carries a single SGD 4.50 cancellation-fee line and nothing else: total_charged is 4.50, payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00, so the whole of the contested SGD 4.50 is the cancellation fee itself and the rider's success on that line is a full refund of it, not a partial one. That line equals trip_record.platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd of 4.50, so there is no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect, and no artifact is impaired under POL-NS-08(a) to (d): the arrived event and the nearest fix agree within 10 seconds, the trace has no gaps across 98 fixes, the chat log's 2 messages match trip_record.chat_message_count of 2, and the fare reconciles. Every artifact this ruling rests on is COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0, so nothing is discounted. Escalation is not engaged: no two admissible artifacts contradict each other on arrival in a way no clause resolves (POL-NS-01(b) and POL-NS-02 settle that question, and the driver accepts limb (b) fails on the trace), the parties' 90-day counterparty dispute counts are both 0, rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 0, the anti-farming check does not trip, and no deciding fact rests on impaired evidence. Ruling. The rider's claim is supported: FULL_REFUND of the SGD 4.50 cancellation fee, with no driver compensation. No clause of the policy in force produces a referral on these facts, so the referrals list is empty. Confidence is 0.95, within the 1.0 cap set by the two weight-1.0 artifacts, EV-GPS-02744 and EV-TRIP-02744, that carry the deciding facts, and above the 0.70 floor. The monetary effect of SGD 4.50 is below the SGD 8.00 automatic-execution threshold, so the refund executes on issue.

His point that no false-arrival finding is available under POL-NS-05 is also accepted: nothing in the derived summary places the driver beyond the 300 m leash or travelling at 15 km/h or more at the 08:11:35 marker, so no false-arrival referral is recorded. The Rider Advocate's grounds (POL-NS-02, POL-NS-06, POL-NS-12) are accepted and are the basis of the refund. Her rider-presence figures are accepted too - 69 fixes from 08:08:52 to 08:19:08, all qualifying, stationary, never more than 13.59 m from the pin - but the ruling does not rest on them; the fee fails on the driver's own position. POL-NS-04 does not exonerate the rider, because her single message 'ok' states no position, entrance or coordinating content and POL-NS-04(a) fails at its first limb; the refund does not depend on that clause. The driver's statement that he 'was right at the pin' is contradicted by his own trace and does not establish the arrival; a counterparty statement carries no weight_multiplier and enters neither the minimum nor the maximum of the confidence cap. The missing advisory. EV-ADVIS-02744-01 is MISSING (issue MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight_multiplier 0.0, null payload). Its absence is itself citable and confirms that POL-NS-06(i) cannot be used to sum separate in-geofence intervals; it carries no fact this ruling rests on. Confidence, escalation and referrals. No POL-NS-09 trigger applies: the driver's statement and his trace are resolved by the POL-NS-02 radius test and POL-NS-03 rather than left in conflict, no repeat-party or anti-farming pattern is shown, and no impaired artifact is the sole evidence of a deciding fact. No referral issues: the driver-education referral in POL-NS-01 attaches to a driver whose stationary fixes lie inside the arrival radius, which is not this case, and no other clause on these facts produces one. The monetary effect is SGD 4.50, at or below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold in POL-GEN-05, so the refund executes automatically.
Draft 3 - sampled
This dispute is about the SGD 4.50 no-show cancellation fee on trip TRP-02744 (EV-FARE-02744 carries a single cancellation_fee line of 4.50, payment_status CHARGED; the trip record's platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd is 4.50, so the ledger line reconciles and POL-NS-08(d) is not engaged). The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-02744-01 is MISSING with weight 0.0 (issue MISSING_ARTIFACT); POL-NS-06(i) makes limb (i) unavailable where the advisory is missing, so no in-geofence intervals may be summed - and there are none to sum in any event.
